title: FOIA - FBI - Quincy Jones

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FOIA - FBI - Quincy Jones
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All records relating to or mentioning Quincy Delight Jones Jr. (March 14, 1933 – November 3, 2024), famed Producer, songwriter, and musician (see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quincy_Jones).

Please conduct a thorough search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices - for both main-file records and cross-reference records for all relevant names, individuals, agencies and companies. For reference, the associated file numbers for these records provided by the FBI are: 161-HQ-12494, 100-HQ-127094 Serial HQ1022, 100-HQ-481695 Serial HQ539, 100-HQ-459279, and 105-WF-20251 Serial 24.

Please see the following major news article reporting on Quincy Jones' passing as proof of death: https://www.cnn.com/2024/11/04/entertainment/quincy-jones-obit/index.html

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

J Ader

communications.communication:
Thank you for contacting foipaquestions@fbi.gov.

Please check the status of your FOIPA Request at http://vault.fbi.gov by clicking on “Check Status of Your FOI/PA Request” on the right side of the page, and follow the instructions below.

Check the Status of Your FOIPA Request

If your FOIPA Number is [1195846-0] please enter [1195846-000] into the system. If your FOIPA Number is [1195846-1] please enter [1195846-001] into the system. If you have any questions about the status of your FOIPA request, please e-mail foipaquestions@fbi.gov.

FIND STATUS OF FOIPA- Request statuses are updated weekly

Please enter the whole FOIPA number-Example: [1234567-000]

FOIPA:
Results will show the Request Number, Case Type and Process Description shown below:
FOIPA:
1234567-000
Case Type:
FOIPA
Process Description (Will display the current progress of the request)

The FBI’s FOIPA Program is searching the FBI’s indices for potentially responsive documents.

You may be contacted via formal letter for all fees and/or negotiation issues that may apply.

NOTE: Recent requests are entered into the FOIPA database in the order that they are received. Before you can check the status, you must have received correspondence assigning a FOIPA request number and the information transferred to the online database. Status information is updated weekly. If a request has been closed within the last six months the online database will display the following: The FOIPA number entered has been closed, and appropriate correspondence has been sent to the address on file.


Estimated Dates of Completion
Requests are processed in the order in which they are received through our multi-track processing system, and the FBI receives a voluminous amount of requests on a daily, weekly, monthly, and annual basis.  Requests are divided into two primary tracks--simple (under 50 pages of potentially responsive documents) and complex (over 50 pages of potentially responsive documents).  Our complex requests are further divided into small (51-250 pages), medium (251-500 pages), large (501-4,999), and extra-large (over 5,000 pages) sub-tracks.  Simple track requests typically require the least amount of time to process.  The more potentially responsive pages a request has, the more complex it becomes, greatly increasing the time required for processing. Generally, the larger the file, the longer it takes to process.
Currently, simple track cases average approximately 230 days from the date of receipt for processing.  Complex requests in the small processing track are currently averaging 1,085 days from the date of receipt for processing, those in the medium processing track are currently averaging 1,310 days, those in the large processing track are currently averaging approximately 2,010 days, and those in the extra-large track are averaging 2,370 days  .


Respectfully,

Public Information Officer
FBI - Information Management Division
200 Constitution Drive
Winchester, VA  22602
O: (540) 868-4593
E: foipaquestions@fbi.gov<mailto:foipaquestions@fbi.gov>

Do you have further questions about the FOI/PA process? Visit us at http://www.fbi.gov/foia

Please check the status of your request online at https://vault.fbi.gov/fdps-1/@@search-fdps    Status updates are performed on a weekly basis.

Note:  This is a non-emergency email address.  If this is an emergency, please call 911 directly.  If you need to report a tip for immediate action, please contact FBI Tips at http://tips.fbi.gov/ or reach out to your local field office.

title: Public Records Request — SanJose Generative AI Records

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Public Records Request — SanJose Generative AI Records
communications.communication:
Subject: Public Records Request — AI Chatbot Interaction Logs

April 9, 2026

Public Records Officer
City of San Jose
200 E. Santa Clara Street
San Jose, CA 95113

Dear Public Records Officer,

I am writing on behalf of a team of researchers and journalists from Stanford University, the University of Southern California, KNKX Public Radio and the New York Times. We are studying how government agencies are adopting and using AI tools in their daily work.

We are writing to request records related to San Jose's use of generative AI tools by city employees.

We are requesting the following records:

1. All interaction logs from ChatGPT Teams, Microsoft Copilot, or any other generative AI chatbot tool — including prompts submitted by city employees and responses generated by the AI — for the period from April 1, 2025 through the date this request is processed. We request these records in their native electronic format where available (e.g., HTML exports, JSON, or CSV).

2. Any policies, guidelines, acceptable use policies, or training materials governing city employee use of ChatGPT Teams, Microsoft Copilot, or other generative AI chatbot tools.

3. Any data retention or deletion policies applicable to AI chatbot interaction logs, including any schedules for automatic deletion of interaction data.

4. Administrative usage statistics for ChatGPT Teams and any other generative AI chatbot tools showing number of users, sessions, and queries processed.

We are seeking the substantive content of AI interactions for research purposes. We do not need personally identifying information of individual employees (such as names and email addresses).

San Jose has purchased 89 ChatGPT Teams licenses at $400 per account, spending more than $35,000, for city employees to use generative AI in their work (see Washington Post, "ChatGPT helps write this mayor's speeches. Now he wants a thousand city workers using AI," July 17, 2025, https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2025/07/17/ai-at-work-san-jose-mayor-matt-mahan-chatgpt/2663b12a-6313-11f0-bf70-56d8888ebb94_story.html; see also Fortune, "Liberal mayor proudly outsources part of his job to ChatGPT," July 17, 2025, https://fortune.com/2025/07/17/san-jose-mayor-matt-mahan-uses-chatgpt-ai-to-do-job/). Mayor Matt Mahan has publicly described using ChatGPT for his own work, and by 2026 he aims to have about 15% of the city's nearly 7,000 workers trained to use AI. San Jose has published generative AI guidelines for city employees (see https://www.sanjoseca.gov/your-government/departments-offices/information-technology/itd-generative-ai-guideline) and is a founder of the GovAI Coalition, a network of government agencies promoting responsible AI use (see https://www.sanjoseca.gov/your-government/departments-offices/information-technology/ai-reviews-algorithm-register/govai-coalition).

We note that records of this type have been made available in response to public records requests in other jurisdictions. See Cascade PBS, WA City Officials Are Using ChatGPT to Write Government Documents (Aug. 2025), https://www.cascadepbs.org/news/2025/08/wa-city-officials-are-using-chatgpt-to-write-government-documents/; see also Texas State AI Usage — Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT), MuckRock, https://www.muckrock.com/foi/texas-109/texas-state-ai-usage-texas-department-of-transportation-txdot-196227/#files.

The results of this research will be published in peer-reviewed academic venues and will contribute to public understanding of how public servants interact with AI systems. This request is made by an academic research institution for scholarly, non-commercial purposes; as such, we request a fee waiver or reduction. If a fee waiver is not granted, please inform me of estimated costs before proceeding. I am willing to pay fees up to $20.

I understand that this may be a novel type of records request and I am happy to answer any technical questions. Please feel free to contact me at the email address or phone number below.

Thank you for your time and assistance.

Sincerely,
Alexander Spangher
Postdoctoral Researcher
Stanford University
alexspan@stanford.edu

P.S. To facilitate your response, we note that ChatGPT Teams conversation histories can be exported by workspace administrators through the ChatGPT admin console, or by individual users via Settings > Data Controls > Export Data. For Microsoft Copilot, interaction histories may be available through the Microsoft 365 admin console or the Purview compliance center. We are happy to provide additional technical guidance if that would be helpful.

P.P.S. Under the California Public Records Act, Cal. Gov. Code 6253(c), public records include "any writing containing information relating to the conduct of the public's business prepared, owned, used, or retained by any state or local agency regardless of physical form or characteristics." Cal. Gov. Code 6252(e). AI chatbot interaction logs created or used by city employees in the course of their official duties qualify as public records under this definition. The city's published generative AI guidelines and its procurement of 89 ChatGPT Teams licenses confirm these tools are part of the conduct of public business. Additionally, NARA Bulletin 2023-02 (Jan. 5, 2023), https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/bulletins/2023/2023-02, provides persuasive authority that chats and electronic messages used for government business are likely government records.

communications.subject: RE: California Public Records Act Request #R012347-041626
communications.communication:
Hello City of San Jose,

First, I want to start by thanking you for your responsiveness and the public spirit in which you are approaching our request. I acknowledge we filed an unbounded request!

Just to give you some background of what we are trying to do, here, we are academic researchers and our primary goal is to assess:
  (1) how AI systems are being used in government
  (2) how academia can help improve these systems by (a) building benchmarks (b) outlining future methodological directions.
We hope these directions can mobilize research in academia to build tooling to better meet the needs of government employees and ultimately impact members of the public. Without data, though, it is hard to know where to start.

We started broad because we are afraid to miss key use-cases. However, in order to make this request more tractable, we are more than willing to work cooperatively to narrow down the scope of records we request. We are seeking to obtain chat records from persons in the following roles:
  - Policy/regulatory staff
  - Communications/public affairs
  - Legal/counsel
  - Program/project management
  - Administrative/executive support
  - Technical/IT staff
  - Human resources
  - Budget/finance
  - Field/operations staff
  - Senior leadership

If it is constructive to filter down to chat logs from 10% or 5% of the employees currently in the City of San Jose, as long as they are evenly distributed across these roles, we would accept that constraint. 

We are happy to work on our end to identify particular individuals or let you identify these individuals, whatever is preferred on your end. We are also very amenable to receiving anonymized data — we have no interest in identifying specific people. We are simply interested in analyzing this data and generating aggregated benchmarking around use-cases.

Please let me know at any point if you need more information or clarification, we can set up a phone call or something.

Thanks,
Alex

Sincerely, 
Alexander Spangher 
Postdoctoral Researcher 
Stanford University 
alexspan@stanford.edu 

P.S. To facilitate your response, we note that ChatGPT Teams conversation histories can be exported by workspace administrators through the ChatGPT admin console, or by individual users via Settings > Data Controls > Export Data. City of San Jose

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Sheriff's Department PROTECT Act Policies November 2026 (Middlesex County Sheriff's Office)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:
This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1. Sheriff’s Department policies, memos or other guidance  currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and a federal immigration authority, defined by M.G.L. Acts of 2026 C. 163 § 7 as “the United States Department of Homeland Security, United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement, United States Customs and Border Protection or any successor entity, and any person acting on their behalf.” The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:
A. Fingerprint and other data sharing with the above-named federal entities,
B. Guidance or policies concerning when communication with federal immigration authorities is allowed. This includes policies concerning how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances. This also includes how and under what circumstances department employees are to document and respond to ICE detainer requests and other requests for information.

2. All Sheriff’s Department policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of sheriff department resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies concerning the use of sheriff department parking lots, facility interior, or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.  

3. All training materials the Sheriff’s Department has developed, used or trained employees on from September 4, 2026 through October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026) regarding civil immigration enforcement, communication with federal immigration authorities, or the use of Sheriff’s department resources for federal civil immigration enforcement.

title: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Braintree Police Department)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Braintree Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice

title: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Police Department)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

communications.communication:
Hello,

We have two Public Records request from ICE that were requested during the time of September 4, 2026-October 31, 2026, one of the reports is attached and the other is denied per the Massachusetts Public Records Laws-see exemptions redactions and denials below. All of our policies can be found on our website-this is the link https://www.lexingtonma.gov/371/Police. We submit fingerprints in accordance with federal requirements, we submit them as required by the State Police, but we do not send them directly to Homeland Security or ICE. The only communication with the Lexington Police Department and @ice.dhs.gov are records requests no other direct communication was found.

26-011553 Redacted per Exemption A:
G. L. c. 41, § 97D provides that these records, along with all communications between police officers and victims of such offenses or abuse shall not be public reports and shall be maintained by the police departments in a manner that shall assure their confidentiality. However, this statute also lists groups of people and entities that may access these records, including victims and their attorneys, victim-witness advocates, and law enforcement.


26-006850 Denied per Exemption A:
G. L. c. 41, § 97D provides that these records, along with all communications between police officers and victims of such offenses or abuse shall not be public reports and shall be maintained by the police departments in a manner that shall assure their confidentiality. However, this statute also lists groups of people and entities that may access these records, including victims and their attorneys, victim-witness advocates, and law enforcement.


Exemption A-Juvenile:

    Confidentiality of Juvenile Records: Unlike adult criminal records, juvenile records in Massachusetts are generally confidential. This means they are not accessible to the     public and are only available to specific parties, such as law enforcement, court personnel, and certain government agencies. The confidentiality of these records aims to     protect the juvenile's privacy and future opportunities.

title: Axon Contract and Procurement Materials

communications.subject: Florida Sunshine Law Request: Axon Contract and Procurement Materials
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

The Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) is submitting this request for records under the Florida Sunshine Law related to the acquisition and cost of services and devices provided by Axon and any of its subsidiaries and partners. 

*Background*
Axon (also known as Axon Enterprise, Inc.) is a company that describes itself as providing “public safety technology solutions” to a variety of customers, many of which are law enforcement agencies based in the United States. For reference, Axon’s website is www.axon.com. These “solutions” may be equipment, software, or “artificial intelligence”-driven analysis of video and data. Some examples of equipment, software, and services created and sold by Axon include (but are not limited to):
• the TASER, a conducted energy device
• body-worn cameras (often referred to as “Axon Body”)
• Axon Fusus, a platform used to integrate cameras and other data into a “real-time crime center” (RTCC) 
• Axon 911, an AI-driven assistant platform for dispatchers
• Axon Evidence, a platform to integrate evidence and other information
• Axon Outpost, an automated license plate reader (ALPR) system
• Axon Lightpost, an ALPR system designed for integration with streetlights
• the Axon AI Era Plan, a collection of AI-driven analysis software (www.axon.com/products/axon-ai-era-plan)
• Axon Vision, an AI-driven video analysis system
• Axon Assistant, an AI-driven chatbot
• Axon Draft One, an AI-assisted police report generation feature
• Axon Records, a records management system
• Axon virtual reality training
• Axon Air DFR, a drone-as-first-responder platform, which may also include drones created by a company called Skydio

Axon provides services or devices to the majority of policing agencies in the United States. Axon often “bundles” services and devices into a single contract, makes adjustments and additions to existing agreements for the provision of new goods, and is designated a “sole source provider” during the procurement process. Contracts and agreements may be active for many years and may include “escalator” clauses that describe ongoing and increasing costs for the procurement over the life of the contract.

*Timeframe*
The requested records are all those related to agreements with Axon active during the year 2026, as well as those agreements related to devices, services, and payments to be provided in the future. 

*Requested records*
This public records request is for materials related to the acquisition and cost of services and devices provided by Axon and any of its subsidiaries and partners. 

1. CONTRACT AND AGREEMENTS
All contracts, memorandums of understanding, and any other written agreements between this agency and Axon. Response records included all associated amendments, exhibits, and supplemental and supporting documentation for each agreement, including any amendments and materials generated subsequent to the initial contract agreement. If this agency uses any Axon product, including but not limited to the ones listed above, agreements referencing those products are responsive to this request; this includes all agreements related to “trial” or “free” periods of use. 

2. FINANCIAL AND PROCUREMENT MATERIALS
All relevant procurement and financial documents and agreements, as well as records of financial transactions, exchanges, and obligations relevant to devices and services procured from Axon. Some of these details and documents may be included as part of the Master Services and Purchasing Agreement or related quotes. 
Responsive materials include: 
• quote materials
• invoices and bills
• records describing specific pricing for each associated line item, including the unit price, the quantity procured of each unit, and associated pricing components. If additional products will be procured over the life of the contract, please be sure to provide records that reflect future acquisitions under the agreement and their cost. 
• receipts
• Requests for Proposal to which Axon provided a response
• bidding materials provided by Axon
• justifications for sole source designation (or equivalent designation, if different terminology is used in your jurisdiction) and associated materials. Responsive materials include any letters and drafts provided by Axon, any supporting materials provided by the company, and any related resolutions and materials generated by the jurisdiction in the process of obtaining a sole source designation for Axon. If the company is not subject to competitive purchasing procedures for a reason that is not a “sole source designation” (for example, because the agreement is part of a cooperative or collaborative purchase), please provide records sufficient to show why the company or the contract is not subject to competitive bidding. 
• records sufficient to show the projected ongoing cost of the agreement with Axon
• records reflecting any discounts or other calculations that were figured into the costs associated with this procurement

*Provision of records*
We ask that these materials be provided on a rolling basis; please provide materials to us as your office collects and reviews records. Please contact us for further discussion regarding the search and release of these materials.

*Fees*
In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform us of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. 
This request is not being made for commercial purposes. Please assess fees appropriately in accordance with a public records request being made in the public interest for research and journalism purposes.

*Format of responsive records*
I request that all records be disclosed in their native, digital format and transmitted to us electronically. 

*Contact information*
If you need any more information in order to process the request, or cannot process a portion of the request for any reason, please respond to the email address on this request or “beryl@eff.org”. Please let us know if a phone call will be necessary or desirable; such contact information will be provided upon request.

Thank you very much for your time and help.

Sincerely,
Beryl Lipton

title: Clearview AI: Contracts, Purchases, Vendor Contacts, and Communications (City of Savannah)

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Clearview AI: Contracts, Purchases, Vendor Contacts, and Communications (City of Savannah)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. Any contract, order form, quote, proposal, terms of service, renewal, amendment, or sole-source or procurement justification between the City of Savannah (including the Savannah Police Department) and Clearview AI, Inc. (City Vendor #25565), including the version of the Clearview Terms of Service that applied to each purchase.

2. Purchase and payment records for Clearview AI purchases dated after January 2, 2025, including requisitions, quotes, approvals, purchase orders, invoices, payment records, the service period each invoice covers, and documents showing the budget unit or funding source charged. This includes PO 306567 and Invoice INV-10821 (paid July 3, 2025, charged to unit 102.4122) and PO 50041 and Invoice INV-11697 (paid May 1, 2026). Please also include the requisition, quote, and approval records for PO 115455 (February 7, 2024), if they exist.

3. The vendor registration or setup file for Clearview AI, Inc. (Vendor #25565), including the vendor application, W-9, and contact information for Clearview representatives. Bank account details may be redacted.

4. Email metadata only (sender, all recipients including cc and bcc, subject line, and date and time) for any email to or from an address at the clearview.ai domain in any City email account, from January 1, 2023 through the date of this request, including messages involving Roberto Gomez or Patrick Schoenberg. Please also include calendar metadata (title, date and time, and attendees) for any meeting, call, or demonstration with Clearview.

title: Town of Linn fire/EMS agreement and proposed fire station

communications.subject: Wisconsin Open Records Act Request: Town of Linn fire/EMS agreement and proposed fire station
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Wisconsin Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

fire station
Dear Records Custodian:
Pursuant to Wisconsin’s Public Records Law, Wis. Stat. §§ 19.31–19.39, and the right of access under § 19.35(1), I request copies of the following records held by the City of Lake Geneva, its Fire Department, its Common Council, and its officers and employees. Unless otherwise noted, the relevant time period is January 1, 2024 to the present.
1.	The Fire and Emergency Services Agreement between the Town of Linn and the City of Lake Geneva — every draft, version, and redline, including the version captioned “CLG/TOL Fire EMS Agreement” with a 3/7/2025 update and any executed version — together with all Exhibits (A, B, C, and D).
2.	All supporting documentation for Exhibit C (Administrative Fee), including the worksheets, spreadsheets, and underlying calculations that produce: the $5,098,708 total annual Fire/EMS maintenance budget; the $1,507,232 deduction; the $250,000 capital figure; the $404,392 reduction attributed to the Town of Geneva; and the derivation of the 2.39% North Shore and 17.28% South Shore three-year average call percentages — including the underlying call/incident data and the maps defining the North Shore and South Shore areas referenced in Exhibits C and D.
3.	The most recent three-year rolling call data (the July 1–June 30 “Measurement Period”) used to determine the Town’s share of the LGFD budget, and all quarterly call summary reports exchanged under Section 3(a) of the agreement.
4.	Any studies, analyses, or consultant reports in the City’s possession regarding fire/EMS service to the Town of Linn or fire-station facilities, including any study estimating the cost of a Linn fire station and any regional or county-wide fire/EMS study (e.g., Wisconsin Policy Forum).
5.	All records regarding any proposed new City of Lake Geneva fire station, including feasibility studies; siting or location analyses; architectural or engineering cost estimates; the basis for any stated project cost (including any figure at or near $41 million); financing and bonding analyses; debt-service projections; any determination regarding a referendum; and communications with bond counsel, financial advisors, or underwriters.
6.	Records identifying which entity — the City or the Town — would bear the capital and operating costs of any new or expanded fire station, and any cost-sharing agreement, capital agreement, term sheet, or memorandum of understanding on that subject.
7.	Closed-session and meeting records concerning the Linn agreement and/or any new fire station: agendas, public notices, minutes, roll-call votes, and any materials or packets distributed to the Common Council or any committee or commission — including the “Closed Session Materials” packet dated on or about March 7, 2025 — together with the specific statutory exemption cited as the basis for each closed session.
8.	Communications (emails, letters, memoranda, and text messages) to, from, or among the Mayor, members of the Common Council, the City Administrator, the Fire Chief, and Town of Linn officials concerning the agreement, the Administrative Fee, the call-percentage methodology, or any new fire station.
9.	Any analysis of the City’s added insurance cost or liability exposure attributable to the Linn agreement (Section 13), and any analysis comparing the City’s total cost of serving Linn against the revenue it receives under the agreement.
Format and fees. Please provide responsive records in electronic format (searchable PDF or native file) where they exist electronically, which should minimize reproduction costs. Per § 19.35(3), please notify me in advance if you anticipate fees exceeding $50 so I may narrow or prioritize the request. As this request is made by a news organization for a matter of significant public interest — a multi-decade, multi-million-dollar intergovernmental commitment and a potential public capital expenditure — I also request a reduction or waiver of fees in the public interest under § 19.35(3)(e).
Timing and withholding. Wisconsin law requires a response “as soon as practicable and without delay” (§ 19.35(4)(a)). If any record, or any portion of a record, is withheld or redacted, please provide a written statement of the specific public-policy reasons for the denial as required by § 19.35(4)(b), identify the legal authority relied upon, and release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions. The fact that a record is a draft, or was discussed in closed session, does not render it categorically exempt from disclosure.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Gary Milliette

Hello,

The City is in receipt of your open records request. Please be aware of the following if applicable:
•	The charge for copies of records is 25 cents per side of page.
•	The charge for any other media is at the actual cost.
•	Pursuant to 19.35(3)(f), Wis. Stats., if the amount to be imposed is more than $5.00, the authority may require prepayment. 
•	Pursuant to Section 19.35(3)(c), Wis. Stats., if the cost to locate the record will cost more than $50.00, the authority may require payment of the location costs. 
•	If a record request response is mailed, the authority may charge the actual postage amount, to be paid before mailing.
•	The City is not obligated to provide records in the format requested. Grebner v. Schiebel, 2001 WI App 17, 240 Wis.2d 551.
•	The City is not obligated to provide records in a time frame established by the requester. Reasonableness of the response time is determined by the volume of records requested, the ability to locate the records, review of records for possible redaction, and other work assignments. Journal Times v. City of Racine Bd. of Police & Fire Comm’rs, 2015 WI 56, 362 Wis.2d 577; WIREdata Inc. v. Village of Sussex, 2008 WI 69, 310 Wis.2d 397.
We are in the process of evaluating your request and will provide further information as it becomes available. 

Thank you,

Vanessa Jahns

City of Lake Geneva

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Flock Audit Logs Dunwoody April - June 2024
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Copies of all audit logs, search logs, or usage reports related to your agency's use of Flock "ALPR" systems for the period March 1, 2024 through June 31, 2024. Specifically I would like the "Organization Audit" logs available in the Flock software's "Insights" section, showing records of license plate searches performed by agency personnel, timestamps of searches, user identification information (names, badge numbers, or user IDs), and any associated case numbers or investigation references.

Please provide records in their original electronic format (CSV, Excel, or similar).

To the extent any portion of these records is claimed exempt under the Open Records Act, I request that the exemption be applied at the field or column level rather than by withholding entire logs, consistent with the segregability requirement of O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(b)(1)(A). If a specific field (such as the free-text search justification field) is withheld, please identify which field and the specific statutory basis for withholding it.

communications.subject: Wisconsin Open Records Act Request: LexisNexis Community Crime Map Contributors - Initial Sweep (Madison Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Wisconsin Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

This request is related to the Community Crime Map (CCM) and Accurint, both are products of LexisNexis. You are receiving this request because your agency's name was listed on the crime map available at communitycrimemap.com. We are seeking documents about how your agency integrates with LexisNexis to provide anonymized data to the CCM, and whether your agency shares de-anonymized data with local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies via Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC) or Public Safety Data Exchange (PSDEx). If your agency currently or previously shared data with LexisNexis, please provide the below documents.  

We are requesting:
1) Technical integration documents: Any documents, integrations instructions, tutorials, and similar documents from LexisNexis about how to connect your RMS/CAD/JMS systems to LexisNexis's systems. [Typically held by IT or records systems teams/vendors from when your agency originally integrated with LexisNexis's systems]
2) Agreements: The signed "XML Addendum", Database Interface Agreement, or similar legal agreement that dictates how your agency's data may be used and shared. [Typically held by legal or procurement departments]
3) Shared Data: An export of what data you share with CCM and other law enforcement agencies. This is often called a Data Classification Crime Results sheet. To obtain this, an account admin can click a link on the left-hand side under admin permissions called 'Data Classification Manager.' There is an Export link on the top right of the Data Classification Manager page. Depending on the LexisNexis product(s) you subscribe to, this may have a different name or location. We are looking for the list of data you share with LexisNexis, and who your share it with (CCM only, or also other law enforcement agencies?) [Only an CCM/Accurint Account Administrators can access these documents]

If you want examples of what these documents look like from other agencies, or you would like suggested search terms to find these documents - please don't hesitate to reach out.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

title: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Edgartown Police Department)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Edgartown Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

This request has been issued tracking number 27-FOI-00161.  Please reference this number in all correspondence and communications with this office.

Please see attached. Portions, as well as the other documents you requested, are being withheld under FOIA Exemptions 4,5, and 6.

Exemption 4 of the FOIA protects "trade secrets and commercial or financial information obtained from a person [that is] privileged or confidential."

FOIA Exemption 5 (deliberative process privilege) applies to inter-agency or intra-agency records where, for instance, there is a work product that is in draft format or documents that contain deliberations between parties leading up to a decision.

Exemption 6 protects the privacy interest of individuals, whose substantial interest in personal identity protection outweighs any public interest link in disclosure of information that could be used to identify them.? In cases such as this, the disclosure of the enclosed records “would constitute a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy.”? See e.g., Pierce v. U.S. Air Force, 512 F.3d 184, 191 (5th Cir. 2007) (“To qualify as a similar file under Exemption 6…the information need only ‘appl[y] to the individual.”)??

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All documents pertaining to collaboration between the Department of Defense (DoD)/Dept. of War and "Arctic Extreme." This title appears on a list of 2025 DoD/Dept. of War entertainment industry collaborations released to me through FOIA. The list is attached to this request. Requested documents may include but should not be limited to: script notes; production assistance agreements; photographs; and all records of communications between employees of DoD/Dept. of War and members of the cast, crew, and production company of "Arctic Extreme," including memos, notes of meetings and conference calls, emails, and other forms of communication.

I am the Director of Research Operations at a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization called The Decoding Culture Foundation as well as the editor-in-chief and a contributor to a research magazine published by said foundation titled "Cultural Engineering Studies." These documents will be used for public education and research purposes. I therefore request a waiver of all fees that may otherwise apply. Attached is a document with organization letterhead confirming my position, as well as the organization's 501(c)(3) application and approval form.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Sheriff's Department PROTECT Act Policies November 2026 (Barnstable County Sheriff's Office)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:
This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1. Sheriff’s Department policies, memos or other guidance  currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and a federal immigration authority, defined by M.G.L. Acts of 2026 C. 163 § 7 as “the United States Department of Homeland Security, United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement, United States Customs and Border Protection or any successor entity, and any person acting on their behalf.” The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:
A. Fingerprint and other data sharing with the above-named federal entities,
B. Guidance or policies concerning when communication with federal immigration authorities is allowed. This includes policies concerning how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances. This also includes how and under what circumstances department employees are to document and respond to ICE detainer requests and other requests for information.

2. All Sheriff’s Department policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of sheriff department resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies concerning the use of sheriff department parking lots, facility interior, or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.  

3. All training materials the Sheriff’s Department has developed, used or trained employees on from September 4, 2026 through October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026) regarding civil immigration enforcement, communication with federal immigration authorities, or the use of Sheriff’s department resources for federal civil immigration enforcement.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. Citizens for Juvenile Justice is an independent nonprofit organization working to reform youth serving systems statewide through Massachusetts. We engage in advocacy across the Commonwealth to ensure all youth are treated fairly and equitably regardless of their race, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, disability or immigration status. We plan to use these records to ensure that all people in Massachusetts, including youth, are adequately protected by law enforcement agencies regardless of real or perceived immigration status.  In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.
The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,
Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initiatives 
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org

title: WA ALPR: A: External Access Audit Logs (1/4) (Yakima Police Department)

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: WA ALPR: A: External Access Audit Logs (1/4) (Yakima Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. All system audit logs, as natively maintained in your agency's systems or your vendor's systems, reflecting access to your agency's ALPR system or any system used to store, process, or query ALPR data (e.g., Axon Evidence.com, Flock Safety portal, Motorola/Vigilant), by users affiliated with any agency other than your agency.

2. All system audit logs, as natively maintained, reflecting the Originating Agency Identifier (ORI) or agency name associated with each external query of your agency's ALPR system.

3. All system audit logs, as natively maintained, reflecting the user identifier, badge number, or account name associated with each query of your agency's ALPR system, whether the querying user was internal or external to your agency.

4. All records identifying which external agencies are currently authorized to access, query, or receive data from your agency's ALPR system, including any configuration record, permissions list, access control list, or authorized-agency registry maintained in your ALPR platform.  If this information exists only as a display within a software interface, a screenshot, faithful reproduction, or export of that display to any available file format is an acceptable and required form of production.

Note on vendor-held records: In Rodriguez v. City of Stanwood & Sedro-Woolley (Skagit County Superior Court, Nov. 6, 2025), the court held that ALPR data held by a third-party SaaS vendor on behalf of a government agency is a public record subject to PRA disclosure. Vendor custody does not relieve your agency of its production obligation. Each request below that encompasses vendor-held records is made on this basis. Please retrieve and produce all responsive records held by your ALPR vendor(s) on your agency's behalf.

Note on record creation: I am seeking existing records only. I understand that no agency is required to create a new record in response to a PRA request. However, producing a screenshot or other faithful reproduction of an existing electronic display is not creating a new record — it is reproducing an existing one, in the same manner as photocopying or scanning a paper document. Agencies cannot evade their production obligation by characterizing screenshots of existing system displays as "new records."

I am requesting these records for research and public interest purposes, submitted through MuckRock, a nonprofit journalism platform. I request that your agency consider waiving any fees given that this request is submitted for research and public interest purposes and that electronic production of the requested records should entail minimal or no actual cost under RCW 42.56.120. For any anticipated costs, please notify me before incurring them so that I may prioritize or narrow the request. This notification requirement should not be construed as authorization to delay production of records for which no fee will be incurred pending resolution of fees for other records in this request

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Phil Mocek

Today’s installment of records contains a total of 35 records. The ALPR Hot List Management reports for the dates of 1/1/2025 through the date of your request; and, a variety of screenshots from Axon relating to various settings and user access. Lt. Cavin provided the following additional response during our attempts to find and access audit logs from Axon: As a matter of practice we did not run audits of the AXON system, since officers were rarely searching plates in
that system.  The AXON plate scans were feeding into the FLOCK system so there was no need to run a check in AXON since a FLOCK search would produce records in both systems. 
Regarding Vigilant, previously used for parking citations, Lt. Cavin has provided the following information: When the user docks their computer and logs into the Vigilant system, they drive through the parking lots and the ALPR scans license plates.  They then wait a specified amount of time 1-2 hours depending on the zone, and drive back through.  The system provides an alert through the program if they scan a license plate/vehicle in the same location (parking spot).  The operator then checks to see if the vehicle has a valid parking permit through the city permit system and determines if a citation is necessary. The data collected by the Vigilant ALPR is stored locally on the hard drive in the patrol vehicle, and is not uploaded to any server or system that would allow for searches.

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1) All MOUs, contracts, addendums, or other legal documents signed by your agency and LexisNexis (and subsidiaries, including LexisNexis Risk Solutions, Accurint, AVCC, PSDEX, etc.). This may include (but is not limited to) a LexisNexis Consortium Sub-Agency Addendum, Schedule A, or other agreements.
2) Any MOUs or other agreements between your agency and CVISS or Sacramento County Sheriff related to sharing RMS/CAD data.
3) Agency Configuration Page: A printout of your agency's AVCC configuration page. Please include the full page, including any other agencies listed on the same page. Example Screenshot: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1G_J35fnmu7qZO_k8UOoVHFcd_R2HKXVg/view?usp=sharing

Context: We understand that CVISS moved to the LexisNexis Accurint platform to share data among CVISS member agencies. We are seeking to understand whether your agency and other CVISS members share contributed data with agencies beyond the consortium (e.g., the Public Safety Data Exchange / PSDEX national database), or whether data sharing is restricted to CVISS members only. Often LexisNexis Sub-Agency Addendums allow agencies to choose whether they share nationally or only within the consortium - we seek to understand what your agency chose to do.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

title: Winchester VA - ALPR contracts, policies, and logs

communications.subject: Virginia Freedom of Information Act Request: Winchester VA - ALPR contracts, policies, and logs
communications.communication:
November 16, 2026
Lieutenant Michael Ackerman 
Winchester Police Department
Re: Freedom of Information Act Request - ALPR contracts, policies, and logs

Pursuant to the Virginia Freedom of Information Act § 2.2-3700., I request copies of the following public records maintained by the Winchester Police Department.

Herein the term “ALPR” refers to both License Plate Reader (LPR) and Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) technology.

1. All contracts, purchase orders, or agreements between the department and Axon Enterprise, Inc, or any affiliated entity, for ALPR technology, including any amendments, renewals, or statements of work. 

2. All data-sharing agreements, memoranda of understanding, or interoperability agreements between the department and any federal agency, state agency, or private entity governing access to or use of ALPR data created by the department.

3. A complete count or inventory of ALPR cameras, both fixed and mobile, currently deployed or operated by the department (regardless of manufacturer and vendor), including location and installation date for each.

4. All written policies, procedures, general orders, or directives governing the use, access, retention, and auditing of ALPR data by department personnel, including any policies on sharing data with outside agencies.

5. All audit logs, access logs, or query records reflecting searches of the ALPR system conducted by department personnel or by outside agencies with access, including the identity of the querying officer or agency, the queried plate or hotlist, and the stated reason for the search where recorded.

For each item, the period covered is November 1, 2025 through present.

Please produce records in electronic format, native where feasible. For item 5, please produce the audit and query records as a native electronic export from the system, in CSV or Excel, rather than as a printout or a summary.

I ask that fees be reduced or waived under § 2.2-3704. The primary purpose of this request is to disseminate the information to the general public, and it is not for commercial use. If the estimated fee will exceed $25.00, please send me an itemized estimate before you begin processing. To the extent any portion of a record is exempt, please release the non-exempt portions and identify the specific exemption claimed for anything withheld, as § 2.2-3704.01 requires. If no records exist, please provide a written certification rather than leaving the item unanswered. Please deliver records electronically via email. 

Virginia FOIA requires a response within five business days of receipt, with one possible extension of seven business days upon written notice stating the reason.

If any part of this request is unclear, please tell me in writing and I will work with you on it.

Sincerely,

Mathew James
103 Winton Lane
Stephens City VA 22655

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Hawaii Uniform Information Practices Act, I hereby request the following records:

The database or records of all law enforcement agencies deaths-in-custody up to the date this request is ultimately fulfilled, including all deaths-in-custody reported pursuant to federal legislation (34 U.S.C. § 60105), as well as all data dictionaries, database scheme documentation or other documentation on the collection and organization of the data. 

I request these records in their native digital formats and not in formats that degrade the accessibility of the records, such as tabular data converted to PDF or Word files. If converting the native digital format to another high-fidelity format, such as CSV or Excel, please take care not to introduce formatting inconsistencies or errors, which can occur in the conversion process (for example, encoding errors or the inclusion of internal unescaped quotation marks in CSV files). Should the records above represent certain values as numeric codes or abbreviations that are not self-explanatory, we additionally request all records necessary to interpret those codes and abbreviations.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Dillon Bergin

title: Granules Pharmaceuticals Inc., FEI 3011585184 — July 2022 and December 2023 Inspection Records and Corrective Actions

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Granules Pharmaceuticals Inc., FEI 3011585184 — July 2022 and December 2023 Inspection Records and Corrective Actions
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

FDA inspections of the following drug manufacturing establishment:

Firm: Granules Pharmaceuticals Inc.
FEI: 3011585184
Address: 3701 Concorde Parkway, Chantilly, VA 20151
Inspection end dates: July 22, 2022, and December 15, 2023
Program area: Human drug manufacturing / current good manufacturing practices (CGMP)

For each inspection, I request:

The final Establishment Inspection Report (EIR), including available exhibits, attachments, and inspectional findings.

The firm's written response to FDA Form 483, including initial responses, supplemental responses, and corrective and preventive action (CAPA) plans submitted to FDA.

Documentation submitted by the firm supporting implementation or completion of proposed corrective actions, including relevant root-cause analyses, revised procedures, investigation summaries, effectiveness checks, and supporting correspondence.

FDA's written evaluations or assessments of the firm's responses and proposed corrective actions, including records indicating whether the responses were considered adequate, inadequate, or in need of further verification.

Correspondence between FDA and Granules Pharmaceuticals concerning the cited deficiencies, corrective actions, implementation deadlines, follow-up inspections, and verification of corrective actions.

Final inspection classification records and associated classification memoranda, including any records explaining the basis for the final classification or subsequent compliance decisions.

For item 5, please search correspondence dated July 22, 2022, through December 31, 2024, relating to either inspection.

I am particularly interested in records concerning manufacturing controls, quality assurance, laboratory testing, investigations of deviations, and deficiencies potentially affecting extended-release pharmaceutical products.

Please provide all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions of responsive records. If any information is withheld, please identify the applicable FOIA exemption and provide sufficient information to describe the withheld material.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emma Yasinski

03/13/2025 

Andrew  Free 
MuckRock News, DEPT MR182997 
Boston, Massachusetts 02115 

RE:	ICE FOIA Case Number 2025-ICFO-25070 
 
Dear Requester: 

This acknowledges receipt of your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), dated 3/13/2025, your request for a waiver of all assessable FOIA fees, and your request for expedited treatment. Your request was received in this office on 3/13/2025. Specifically, you have requested records pertaining to a copy of the IHSC Mortality Review for Ousmane Ba, who died in ICE Custody February 23, 2024, according to the Detainee Death Report ICE published: https://www.ice.gov/doclib/foia/reports/ddr_OusmaneBa.pdf. 

Due to the increasing number of FOIA requests received by this office, we may encounter some delay in processing your request. Per Section 5.5(a) of the DHS FOIA regulations, 6 C.F.R. Part 5, ICE processes FOIA requests according to their order of receipt. Although ICE’s goal is to respond within 20 business days of receipt of your request, the FOIA does permit a 10-day extension of this time period. As your request seeks numerous documents that will necessitate a thorough and wide-ranging search, ICE will invoke a 10-day extension for your request, as allowed by Title 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B). If you’re able to narrow the scope of your request please contact our office. Narrowing the scope may speed up the search process. We will make every effort to comply with your request in a timely manner. 

ICE evaluates fee waiver requests under the legal standard set forth above and the fee waiver policy guidance issued by the Department of Justice on April 2, 1987, as incorporated into the Department of Homeland Security’s Freedom of Information Act regulations.  These regulations set forth six factors to examine in determining whether the applicable legal standard for fee waiver has been met.  I have considered the following factors in my evaluation of your request for a fee waiver: 

(1) Whether the subject of the requested records concerns “the operations or activities of the government”; 
(2) Whether the disclosure is “likely to contribute” to an understanding of government operations or activities; 
(3) Whether disclosure of the requested information will contribute to the understanding of the public at large, as opposed to the individual understanding of the requestor or a narrow segment of interested persons; 
(4) Whether the contribution to public understanding of government operations or activities will be "significant"; 
(5) Whether the requester has a commercial interest that would be furthered by the requested disclosure; and 
(6) Whether the magnitude of any identified commercial interest to the requestor is sufficiently large in comparison with the public interest in disclosure, that disclosure is primarily in the commercial interest of the requestor. 

Upon review of your request and a careful consideration of the factors listed above, I have determined to grant your request for a fee waiver. 

Your request for expedited treatment is hereby denied. 

Under the DHS FOIA regulations, expedited processing of a FOIA request is warranted if the request involves “circumstances in which the lack of expedited treatment could reasonably be expected to pose an imminent threat to the life or physical safety of an individual,” 6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(1)(i), or “an urgency to inform the public about an actual or alleged federal government activity, if made by a person primarily engaged in disseminating information,” 6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(l)(ii).  Requesters seeking expedited processing must submit a statement explaining in detail the basis for the request, and that statement must be certified by the requester to be true and correct.  6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(3). 

Your request for expedited processing is denied because you do not qualify for either category under 6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(1).  You failed to demonstrate a particular urgency to inform the public about the government activity involved in the request beyond the public’s right to know about government activity generally.  Your letter was conclusory in nature and did not present any facts to justify a grant of expedited processing under the applicable standards. 

If you deem the decision to deny expedited treatment of your request an adverse determination, you have the right to appeal.  Should you wish to do so, you must send your appeal and a copy of this letter, within 90 days of the date of this letter following the procedures outlined in the DHS FOIA regulations at 6 C.F.R. Part 5 § 5.5(e)(2). You may submit your appeal electronically at GILDFOIAAppeals@ice.dhs.gov or via regular mail to: 

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement 
Office of the Principal Legal Advisor 
U.S. Department of Homeland Security 
500 12th Street,, S.W., Mail Stop 5900 
Washington, D.C. 20536-5900 

Your envelope and letter should be marked “FOIA Appeal.”  Copies of the FOIA and DHS regulations are available at www.dhs.gov/foia. 

ICE has queried the appropriate program offices within ICE for responsive records. If any responsive records are located, they will be reviewed for determination of releasability. Please be assured that one of the processors in our office will respond to your request as expeditiously as possible. We appreciate your patience as we proceed with your request. 

If you have any questions please contact FOIA Public Liaison Daniel Edgington, at (866) 633-1182 or 500 12th St, SW Stop 5009 Washington, DC 20536-5009. Additionally, you have a right to seek dispute resolution services from the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) which mediates disputes between FOIA requesters and Federal agencies as a non-exclusive alternative to litigation.  If you are requesting access to your own records (which is considered a Privacy Act request), you should know that OGIS does not have the authority to handle requests made under the Privacy Act of 1974.  You may contact OGIS as follows:  Office of Government Information Services, National Archives and Records Administration, 8601 Adelphi Road-OGIS, College Park, Maryland 20740-6001, e-mail at ogis@nara.gov; telephone at 202-741-5770; toll free at 1-877-684-6448. 

Your request has been assigned reference number 2025-ICFO-25070. Please use this number in future correspondence. 

Sincerely, 

ICE FOIA Office 
Immigration and Customs Enforcement 
Freedom of Information Act Office 
500 12th Street, S.W., Stop 5009 
Washington, D.C. 20536-5009
